metadata.title: Repository for the formalization of A∞ categories, following Seidel's book.

nodes.name: Grading type
nodes.statement: A grading type is an abelian group $\beta$ together with group homomorphisms \[ \operatorname{shift} : \mathbb{Z} \to \beta, \qquad \operatorname{sign} : \beta \to \{\pm 1\}, \] such that $\operatorname{sign}(\operatorname{shift}(1)) = -1$; that is, the differential, which has degree $\operatorname{shift}(1)$, is odd. For a degree $d \in \beta$ we write $(-1)^d := \operatorname{sign}(d)$ for its Koszul sign.
nodes.label: AInfinityTheory.GradingType

nodes.name: Sign of an integer shift
nodes.statement: For every integer $n$ one has $(-1)^{\operatorname{shift}(n)} = (-1)^n$.
nodes.label: AInfinityTheory.sign_shift

nodes.statement: Since $\operatorname{shift}(n) = n \cdot \operatorname{shift}(1)$ and $\operatorname{sign}$ is a homomorphism, $(-1)^{\operatorname{shift}(n)} = \operatorname{sign}(\operatorname{shift}(1))^n = (-1)^n$.

nodes.name: Standard gradings
nodes.statement: The integers $\mathbb{Z}$ form a grading type with $\operatorname{shift}$ the identity and $\operatorname{sign}(n) = (-1)^n$. The parities $\mathbb{Z}/2$ form a grading type with $\operatorname{shift}$ the reduction modulo $2$ and $\operatorname{sign}(p) = (-1)^p$.
nodes.label: AInfinityTheory.GradingType.standard

nodes.name: Product gradings
nodes.statement: Let $\beta$ be a grading type and $\gamma$ an abelian group. The product $\beta \times \gamma$ is a grading type with $\operatorname{shift}(n) = (\operatorname{shift}(n), 0)$ in two ways: either the sign is read off the first factor alone, $\operatorname{sign}(b,c) = (-1)^b$, or, when $\gamma$ is a grading type as well, the sign is the total sign $\operatorname{sign}(b,c) = (-1)^b\,(-1)^c$. Neither choice is canonical, so both are constructions to be activated locally rather than instances.
nodes.label: AInfinityTheory.GradingType.prod

nodes.name: Graded linear map
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a semiring and let $M, N$ be $\beta$-indexed families of $R$-modules. A graded $R$-linear map $f : M \to N$ of degree $d \in \beta$ consists of an $R$-linear map $f_{i,j} : M(i) \to N(j)$ for every pair of degrees with $i + d = j$. Graded linear maps of degree $d$ form an $R$-module under componentwise operations.
nodes.label: AInfinityTheory.GradedLinearMap

nodes.name: Composition of graded linear maps
nodes.statement: The composite of graded linear maps of degrees $d$ and $e$ is a graded linear map of degree $d + e$, whose component from degree $i$ factors through degree $i + d$. The identity is a graded linear map of degree $0$. Composition is associative and unital.
nodes.label: AInfinityTheory.GradedLinearMap.comp

nodes.statement: Componentwise, this is associativity and unitality of composition of linear maps, once every component of a composite is seen to factor through any middle degree.

nodes.name: Graded multilinear map
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a semiring, let $(M_j)_{j \in \iota}$ be a finite family of $\beta$-indexed families of $R$-modules, and let $N$ be a $\beta$-indexed family of $R$-modules. A graded $R$-multilinear map of degree $d \in \beta$ consists, for every choice of input degrees $(d_j)_{j \in \iota}$ and every output degree $i$ with $\sum_j d_j + d = i$, of an $R$-multilinear map \[ \prod_j M_j(d_j) \to N(i). \] Graded multilinear maps of degree $d$ form an $R$-module under componentwise operations.
nodes.label: AInfinityTheory.GradedMultilinearMap

nodes.name: Graded linear quiver
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring $R$, a graded $R$-linear quiver on an object type $\mathrm{Obj}$ assigns to each pair of objects $(X,Y)$ and each degree $i \in \beta$ an $R$-module $\operatorname{Hom}(X,Y)_i$ of morphisms of degree $i$ from $X$ to $Y$.
nodes.label: AInfinityTheory.GradedLinearQuiver

nodes.name: Operation target degree
nodes.statement: Given input degrees $(d_0,\dots,d_{n-1})$ in a grading type $\beta$, the output degree of the $n$-ary operation is \[ \sum_i d_i + \operatorname{shift}(2-n), \] where the final summand is the image of the integer $2-n$ under the shift homomorphism $\mathbb{Z} \to \beta$.
nodes.label: AInfinityTheory.operationTargetDeg

nodes.name: Stasheff target degree
nodes.statement: The common degree of the arity-$n$ Stasheff relation is \[ \sum_i d_i + \operatorname{shift}(3-n) \] in the grading type.
nodes.label: AInfinityTheory.stasheffTargetDeg

nodes.name: Composable morphism type
nodes.statement: For a string of objects $X_0,\dots,X_n$, an index $i < n$ and a degree $b$, this is the hom-module $\operatorname{Hom}(X_i, X_{i+1})_b$ of the $i$-th morphism in that composable string, in degree $b$.
nodes.label: AInfinityTheory.GradedLinearQuiver.ComposableHomType

nodes.name: \Ainf{}-composition
nodes.statement: An \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{A_\infty}}{A-infinity}{}-composition on a graded quiver $\operatorname{Hom}$ assigns to every positive arity $n$ and every string of objects $X_0,\dots,X_n$ a graded multilinear map \[ m_n : \operatorname{Hom}(X_0,X_1) \times \cdots \times \operatorname{Hom}(X_{n-1},X_n) \to \operatorname{Hom}(X_0,X_n) \] of degree $\operatorname{shift}(2-n)$. Thus for input degrees $(d_0,\dots,d_{n-1})$ its component lands in any degree equal to the operation target degree.
nodes.label: AInfinityTheory.AInfinityComposition

nodes.name: Indexed Stasheff term
nodes.statement: Fix an \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{A_\infty}}{A-infinity}{}-composition $m$. For $r + s + t = n$ with $s \geq 1$, is the term obtained by first applying the inner $s$-ary operation in positions $r,\dots,r+s-1$ and then applying the outer $(r+1+t)$-ary operation to the collapsed string. It lies in $\operatorname{Hom}(X_0,X_n)$ in any degree equal to the Stasheff target degree.
nodes.label: AInfinityTheory.indexedStasheffTerm

nodes.name: Stasheff sign
nodes.statement: The sign $\pm 1$ attached to $(r,s,t)$ is \[ \prod_{k=r+s}^{n-1} (-1)^{\|a_k\|}, \qquad \|a_k\| := |a_k| - \operatorname{shift}(1), \] the product of the Koszul signs of the reduced degrees of the $t$ trailing inputs. Since the sign character is a homomorphism, this equals $(-1)^{|a_{r+s}| + \cdots + |a_{n-1}| - \operatorname{shift}(t)}$.
nodes.label: AInfinityTheory.stasheffSign

nodes.name: Indexed Stasheff sum
nodes.statement: The arity-$n$ Stasheff sum is the signed sum of all valid composites of an inner operation followed by an outer operation, that is, of the Stasheff terms indexed by $0 \leq r \leq n$ and $1 \leq s \leq n - r$, with $t = n - r - s$. It lies in $\operatorname{Hom}(X_0,X_n)$ in any degree equal to the Stasheff target degree.
nodes.label: AInfinityTheory.indexedStasheffSum

nodes.name: Indexed Stasheff identities
nodes.statement: An \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{A_\infty}}{A-infinity}{}-composition satisfies the Stasheff identities if every indexed Stasheff sum vanishes, for every positive arity, string of objects, choice of input degrees and composable inputs.
nodes.label: AInfinityTheory.indexedSatisfiesStasheff

nodes.name: \Ainf{}-precategory
nodes.statement: An \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{A_\infty}}{A-infinity}{}-precategory over $R$ with object type $\mathrm{Obj}$ consists of a graded $R$-linear quiver \[ \operatorname{Hom} : \mathrm{Obj} \to \mathrm{Obj} \to \operatorname{grMod}_R^\beta \] together with an \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{A_\infty}}{A-infinity}{}-composition, that is, operations \[ m_n : \operatorname{Hom}(X_0, X_1) \otimes \dots \otimes \operatorname{Hom}(X_{n-1}, X_n) \to \operatorname{Hom}(X_0, X_n) \] of degree $\operatorname{shift}(2-n)$ for every positive arity $n>0$. No relations are imposed on these composition maps.
nodes.label: AInfinityTheory.AInfinityCategoryStruct

nodes.name: Chain
nodes.statement: A chain in an \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{A_\infty}}{A-infinity}{}-precategory consists of a positive length $n$, a string of $n+1$ objects, and a degree assigned to each of the $n$ composable morphism slots.
nodes.label: AInfinityCategoryTheory.AInfinityPreCategory.Chain

nodes.name: Chain source
nodes.statement: The source of a chain is its initial object.
nodes.label: AInfinityCategoryTheory.AInfinityPreCategory.Chain.source

nodes.name: Chain target
nodes.statement: The target of a chain is its final object.
nodes.label: AInfinityCategoryTheory.AInfinityPreCategory.Chain.target

nodes.name: Chain link type
nodes.statement: For a chain and an index $i$, \texttt{Chain.link} is the module of the $i$-th composable morphism in that chain.
nodes.label: AInfinityCategoryTheory.AInfinityPreCategory.Chain.link

nodes.name: Chain operation target
nodes.statement: For a chain, this is the graded hom-module that receives the corresponding multilinear operation.
nodes.label: AInfinityCategoryTheory.AInfinityPreCategory.Chain.operationTarget

nodes.name: \Ainf{}-category
nodes.statement: An \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{A_\infty}}{A-infinity}{}-category is an \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{A_\infty}}{A-infinity}{}-precategory together with a proof that its operations satisfy the Stasheff identities.
nodes.label: AInfinityTheory.AInfinityCategory

nodes.name: Stasheff sum vanishes in an \Ainf{}-category
nodes.statement: For an \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{A_\infty}}{A-infinity}{}-category, every Stasheff sum computed from the structure maps is equal to zero.
nodes.label: AInfinityTheory.AInfinityCategory.indexedStasheffSum_eq_zero

nodes.statement: This is the Stasheff identity that is part of the data of an \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{A_\infty}}{A-infinity}{}-category.

nodes.name: \Ainf{}-algebra structure
nodes.statement: Let $A$ be a graded $R$-module. An \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{A_\infty}}{A-infinity}{}-algebra structure on $A$ consists of multilinear operations \[ m_n : A(d_0) \otimes \cdots \otimes A(d_{n-1}) \to A\!\left(\sum_i d_i + \operatorname{shift}(2 - n)\right) \] for every positive arity $n$ and every choice of input degrees.
nodes.label: AInfinityAlgebraTheory.AInfinityAlgStruct

nodes.name: Algebra to precategory
nodes.statement: Any \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{A_\infty}}{A-infinity}{}-algebra structure determines a one-object \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{A_\infty}}{A-infinity}{}-precategory, with object type and constant hom-module equal to the underlying graded module.
nodes.label: AInfinityAlgebraTheory.AInfinityAlgStruct.toPreCategory

nodes.name: Algebra Stasheff sum
nodes.statement: The Stasheff sum of an \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{A_\infty}}{A-infinity}{}-algebra is the Stasheff sum of its associated one-object \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{A_\infty}}{A-infinity}{}-precategory.
nodes.label: AInfinityAlgebraTheory.AInfinityAlgStruct.stasheffSum

nodes.name: Algebra Stasheff property
nodes.statement: An \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{A_\infty}}{A-infinity}{}-algebra structure satisfies the Stasheff identities when every one of its Stasheff sums is zero.
nodes.label: AInfinityAlgebraTheory.AInfinityAlgStruct.satisfiesStasheff

nodes.name: \Ainf{}-algebra
nodes.statement: An \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{A_\infty}}{A-infinity}{}-algebra is an \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{A_\infty}}{A-infinity}{}-algebra structure together with a proof of the Stasheff identities.
nodes.label: AInfinityAlgebraTheory.AInfinityAlgebra

nodes.name: Stasheff sum vanishes in an \Ainf{}-algebra
nodes.statement: For an \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{A_\infty}}{A-infinity}{}-algebra, every algebraic Stasheff sum is equal to zero.
nodes.label: AInfinityAlgebraTheory.AInfinityAlgebra.stasheff_eq_zero

nodes.name: \Ainf{}-algebra to precategory
nodes.statement: An \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{A_\infty}}{A-infinity}{}-algebra canonically determines a one-object \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{A_\infty}}{A-infinity}{}-precategory.
nodes.label: AInfinityAlgebraTheory.AInfinityAlgebra.toPreCategory

nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a preadditive category. Then the \emph{computable additive completion} of $\mathcal{C}$, denoted $\operatorname{CMat}(\mathcal{C})$, has \begin{itemize} \item as objects, lists of elements in $\mathcal{C}$. \item as morphisms, dependent matrices of morphisms in $\mathcal{C}$. Specifically, if $(A_0, A_1, \ldots, A_n), (B_0, B_1, \ldots, B_m) \in \operatorname{Ob}\big(\operatorname{Mat\_}(\mathcal{C})\big)$, then \begin{multline*} \operatorname{Hom}\big((A_0, A_1, \ldots, A_n), (B_0, B_1, \ldots, B_m)\big) \\ = \left\{ \begin{bmatrix} a_{00} & \cdots & a_{0,n-1} \\ \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ a_{m-1,0} & \cdots & a_{m-1,n-1} \end{bmatrix} : a_{ij} \in \operatorname{Hom}(A_j, B_i) \right\} \end{multline*} where $0 \le i \le m-1$ and $0 \le j \le n-1$. \item composition is defined by matrix multiplication \item identities are given by the identity matrix $$ (\mathbb{1}_{(A_0, \ldots, A_m)})_{i, j} = \begin{cases} \mathbb{1}_{A_i} & \text{reinterpreted as an element of }\operatorname{Hom}(A_i, A_j) \text{ by casting along the equality if }i = j \\ 0 & \text{ if }i\ne j \end{cases}$$. \end{itemize}

Given $A = (A_0, \ldots, A_n), B=(B_0, \ldots, B_n)\in \operatorname{CMat\_}(\mathcal{C})$, the \emph{computable biproduct} of $A$ and $B$ is defined by $A\boxplus_k B = (A_0, \ldots, A_n, B_0, \ldots, B_m)$

For any $Z\in \operatorname{CMat\_} (\mathcal{C})$, the \emph{index type}, denoted $\iota_Z$, is the type $\{ 0, \ldots, (\operatorname{len}(Z)-1)\}$, and the indexing function, $X_2: \iota_Z\to \mathcal{C}$, is defined by $X_Z(i) = Z_i$.

Let $n\in \mathbb{N}$. A \emph{positioning} of $1$ black strand with $n$ red strands is an element of $\{0, \ldots, n+1\}$. Given positionings of $X$ and $Y$, the strand set $StrandSpace_{X, Y} = \mathbb{N}$, representing the number of dots. (Note here that $\text{StrandSpace}_{X, Y}$ does not depend on $X$ or $Y$, but with more black strands it might).

If $X, Y, Z$ are positionings of $1$ black strand and $n$ red strands and $a\in \text{StrandSpace}_{X, Y}$, $b\in \text{StrandSpace}_{Y, Z}$, then their composition is given by \begin{align*} b\circ a &= a + b + \frac{|X-Y| + |Y-Z| - |X-Z|}{2} \\ &= a + b + \max (x, y) + \max (y, z) - \max (x, z) - y \end{align*}

Fix a commutative ring $R$. The $\operatorname{KLRW}$ category of $1$ black strand and $n$ red strands, denoted $\operatorname{KLRW}$ category of $1$ black strand and $n$ red strands, denoted $\operatorname{KLRW}^R_n$, is given by \begin{itemize} \item $\operatorname{Ob}(\operatorname{KLRW}^R_n)$ is the set of positionings of $1$ black strand with $n$ red strands \item $\operatorname{Hom}(X, Y)$ is the free $R$-module generated by $\text{StrandSpace}_{X, Y}$. \end{itemize} Composition in $\operatorname{KLRW}^R_n$ is defined by extending the composition of elements of the strand space linearly. Since each $\operatorname{Hom}(X, Y)$ is an $R$-module and composition is $R$-linear, $\operatorname{KLRW}^R_n$ is $R$-linear and thus preadditive.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a preadditive category with a zero object. Then a bounded cochain complex of $\mathcal{C}$ is a ($\mathbb{Z}$-graded) cochain complex $A^\bullet$ of $\mathcal{C}$ equipped with a finite set $S$ called the support, satisfying $\forall i\in \mathbb{Z}, i\in S \Leftrightarrow A^i\not\cong 0$. Note that $S$ is uniquely determined by $A^\bullet$, though included for computability.

Let $\operatorname{BK}^\bullet(\mathcal{C})$ denote the set of bounded cochain complexes in $\mathcal{C}$. THen there is a function $F:\operatorname{BK}^\bullet(\mathcal{C})\to K^\bullet(\mathcal{C})$ which forgets the finiteness. Then we equip $\operatorname{BK}^\bullet(\mathcal{C})$ with the induced category structure of $F$ which makes $F$ into a fully faithful functor $F:\operatorname{BK}^\bullet(\mathcal{C}) \to K^\bullet (\mathcal{C})$.
This axiom is automatic from the typing of $\beta_1$: its codomain consists of morphisms of cochain complexes, which by definition commute with differentials.

Since $\beta_2$ produces degree $-1$ maps, their composition has degree $-2$. This axiom says this composition vanishes. For $n \geq 5$, all $[\mathrm{SF}_n]$ axioms are identically zero because every term involves either $\beta_k$ with $k \geq 3$ or $\mu_k$ with $k \geq 3$, both of which are zero.
